files_changed.summary: LLM interface: Complete(ctx, prompt string) (string, error). Retriever/Memory/Personas intentionally not added — unused until a later stage needs them.
runAnalytic(ctx, llm, runID, content) — one LLM.Complete call wrapped as a single root Point via NewPoint.

StartRunCmd (SessionID, Mode, Content), Service (llm, clock, in-memory runs map + mutex), NewService, StartRun (validates Content, creates+starts Run, advances past scope_anchor, runs analytic stub, advances past analytic on success or Fails the run on LLM error, records state), RunState accessor for callers/tests.

decisions: No Store interface (confirmed with user): Service keeps run/point state in an internal map[RunID]*runRecord guarded by a mutex, exposed only via RunState(). Avoids a single-implementation interface; store.go/store_pg.go come with whatever future task actually persists to Postgres.
StartRunCmd.Content added (confirmed with user): analytic needs input and no memory/message layer exists yet to source it.

scope_anchor is handled by one Run.Advance() call with no stage handler or persisted work, since Run.Start() always sets the cursor to Order[0] (task 007 invariant) and the real context-warning gate is a later task (build order step 9).

No orchestrator.go or stages/ subpackage: sequencing (Start -> Advance -> analytic -> Advance) is inline in StartRun. Same reasoning as task 006's deferred stages/ subpackage — one handler doesn't justify the generic Stage->Handler dispatch machinery, and it would reintroduce the Stage-type import-cycle problem noted there.

On LLM failure, StartRun still returns the created run's (now failed) RunID alongside the error, rather than an empty ID — the run row conceptually exists and is marked failed, so a caller/test can still look it up via RunState. Deviates slightly from the 'zero value on error' Go convention but matches the domain: the resource was created before the failure.
runAnalytic always produces exactly one Point regardless of LLM output content — real multi-point decomposition depends on internal/llm's actual response contract (build order step 6, not yet built).
